title: 2 of Eden's 4 Rivers Are Real
author: QUILL
notes: All Eden locations are proposals. Pishon/Gihon unidentified. Not-proven line in beat 9.

beats.text: Two of Eden's four rivers are real.
Genesis 2 names four. The last clue is one Sumerian word.
beats.say: Genesis 2 names four. The last clue is one soo-MARE-ee-an word.

beats.text: Two are real: the Tigris and Euphrates, both flowing through Iraq today.
beats.say: Two are real: the TY-gris and the yoo-FRAY-teez, both flowing through Iraq today.

beats.text: But Pishon and Gihon were never securely identified.
beats.say: But PIE-shon and GEE-hon were never securely identified.

beats.text: Proposal one: dried riverbeds now buried beneath the Persian Gulf.
Proposal two looks north, where both rivers begin. Eden at either end?
beats.label: NORTH OR SOUTH?

beats.text: At al-Qurnah, where the rivers meet, locals show a tree called Adam's.
beats.say: At al-KOOR-nah, where the rivers meet, locals show a tree called Adam's.

beats.text: Here's the last clue: some scholars link Eden to Sumerian edin, meaning plain.
beats.say: Here's the last clue: some scholars link Eden to Sumerian EH-din, meaning plain.
beats.label: EDIN = PLAIN?

beats.text: Not proven: Eden's location. These are proposals, not discoveries.
Real rivers, a lost garden, one Sumerian word.
beats.say: Real rivers, a lost garden, one soo-MARE-ee-an word.

beats.text: Two of Eden's four rivers are real. So Iraq, or Armenia?

Genesis 2 names four rivers. Two flow through Iraq today, two are still unidentified, and one Sumerian word may be the last clue.
Every Eden location is a proposal, not a discovery.
